Case study 11 · Apollo Group · Platform Control

Apollo GroupLearning Platform

Product Manager for the admin console that let dozens of schools run online programs without a developer on call.

Scroll the story

Role

Product Manager; vision and design for the entire admin area

Timeline

Grew with each tenant school

Team

The short version

01

The problem

Apollo wanted a classroom in a box for smaller schools, a new revenue stream. Configuring a school meant scripts and institutional memory.

02

What I owned

Vision and design for the entire administrative area, from requirements to the console.

03

The approach

Build versus buy, then contextual inquiry in IT control centers. Verdict: an MVP that grows with each client, with a course builder that follows how faculty already work.

04

The result

Non-technical staff took over work that used to need developers. The platform ran dozens of schools and still serves some of Apollo’s smaller ones.

The platform, start to finish

01

The brief

Package Apollo’s ecosystem as a classroom in a box for smaller schools and open a new revenue stream. As Product Manager I owned vision and design for the entire administrative area.

02

Requirements

Gathered use cases from DevOps, engineering, IT and curriculum teams and translated them into user stories and wireframes. The console had to configure dozens of tenant schools for semi-technical admins.

03

Scope

Enrollment, assessment, placement, classroom creation, analytics and legacy SIS integration in one console, replacing scripts held together by institutional memory.

04

Research

Build versus buy through vendor analysis, then contextual inquiry in IT control centers. Verdict: build an MVP and grow it with each client.

05

Curriculum design

Faculty and curriculum designers mapped how courses actually get made. The course builder followed that process instead of asking them to adopt a new one.

06

Roles and users

Super-admin course views across institutions, role and permission management, and class assignment that could override legacy systems for clients without a student information system.

07

Result

Non-technical staff took over daily tasks that used to need developers. The platform went on to run dozens of tenant schools and still serves some of Apollo’s smaller ones.
